hypotheses.title: Queued Hook Fee Execution Clears Reentrancy Flags — Creates Unguarded Re-entry Window via Token Callbacks
hypotheses.mechanism: In _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers (AMMModule.sol:3183-3204), line 3190 calls _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS). Per TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol:68-72, _setReentrancyFlags strips ENTERED and NOT_ENTERED bits from `flags` (yielding 0) then preserves only the ENTERED bit from current state. Result: the guard value becomes `ENTERED` (0x02) — ALL specific flags (SWAP_GUARD_FLAG=0x04, LIQUIDITY_GUARD_FLAG=0x80, FLASHLOAN_GUARD_FLAG=0x800) are CLEARED. The function then iterates queued transfers (lines 3192-3201), each calling _transferHookFeesByHook which does SafeERC20.safeTransfer (line 3133). If the fee token implements transfer callbacks (ERC-777 tokensReceived, or ERC-20 with hooks), the recipient contract gains execution. The recipient calls collectHookFeesByHook (ModuleFeeCollection.sol:72). The check at line 75 tests _isReentrancyFlagSet(SWAP_GUARD_FLAG) — returns FALSE (flag cleared). Line 77 tests FLASHLOAN_GUARD_FLAG — also FALSE. Execution falls through to line 79-80: _transferHookFeesByHook(msg.sender, ...) — DIRECT execution, bypassing the intended queueing mechanism. Attack: A hook that collects fees for the SAME hookFeeKey in the callback drains the tokensOwed balance via the direct path. When the loop continues to the original queued entry, _transferHookFeesByHook finds insufficient balance — underflow check at line 3130 triggers revert. Since executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers was called via external CALL at line 2247 (ILimitBreakAMM(address(this)).executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers()), the revert propagates to _finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse, bricking the entire swap. This is a guaranteed DoS vector for any swap that queues hook fees to a recipient contract with transfer callbacks.
grounded_in: code-observation: _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) at AMMModule.sol:3190 — per TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol:69 `flags = flags & ~(ENTERED | NOT_ENTERED)` yields 0, line 70 extracts ENTERED from current, line 71 stores `ENTERED | 0 = ENTERED`. SWAP_GUARD_FLAG (1<<2=4) is NOT in the result. _isReentrancyFlagSet(4) at ModuleFeeCollection.sol:75 returns (2 & 4 > 0) = false.

code-observation: collectHookFeesByHook at ModuleFeeCollection.sol:72-82 has NO nonReentrant modifier — it relies on flag-specific checks (SWAP_GUARD_FLAG, LIQUIDITY_GUARD_FLAG, FLASHLOAN_GUARD_FLAG) which are all cleared, causing fall-through to direct _transferHookFeesByHook at line 80.

EXP-9: Read-only reentrancy pattern variant — state (tokensOwed) is committed before the re-entry opportunity. The queued entries reference committed state that the callback can access and modify through the unguarded collectHookFeesByHook path.

EXP-13: Arbitrary call vulnerability — SafeERC20.safeTransfer at line 3133 transfers control to an arbitrary recipient contract during the flag-cleared window. The transfer target is hook-chosen (queued at line 3174 from _queueTransferHookFeesByHook parameter).
Solodit: Bunni v2 reentrancy lock bypass (Cyfrin audit) — BunniHub.unlockForRebalance() cleared reentrancy protection during hook execution, allowing hooks to re-enter via token callbacks.

coupled_pair.state_a: Reentrancy flags in transient storage — cleared to ENTERED-only at AMMModule.sol:3190
coupled_pair.state_b: tokensOwed[hookFeeKey] in persistent storage — decremented by both queue loop (line 3129) and direct collectHookFeesByHook (same line via callback)
coupled_pair.invariant: Swap-specific reentrancy flags must remain set while AMM state is being mutated during fee distribution

masking_code.masks_invariant: executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers msg.sender==address(this) check (line 128) prevents DIRECT external calls but does not prevent re-entry through token transfer callbacks during the flag-cleared window

hypotheses.title: Output Swap Partial Fill Stores Irrevocable Hook Fees for Non-Actualized Volume
hypotheses.mechanism: In _poolSwapByOutput (AMMModule.sol), _applySwapByOutputOutputFees is called at line 1537 BEFORE the pool type's swapByOutput call at line 1548. Inside _applySwapByOutputOutputFees (lines 2851-2895): tokenInTokenOutFee and tokenOutTokenOutFee (set by beforeSwapHooks) are ADDED to swapAmountOut (lines 2863, 2875), increasing the amount the pool must provide. These hook fees are irrevocably committed to persistent storage via _storeHookFees at lines 2871 and 2887. The inflated amountOut is passed to the pool type. If the pool type returns actualAmountOut < originalAmountOut (partial fill, line 1559), the adjustment at lines 1569-1582 reduces adjustedAmountSpecified (user's output) by amountOutAdjustment = originalAmountOut - actualAmountOut (line 1569). The stored hook fees are NOT proportionally reduced. In contrast, input swap partial fills at lines 1413-1427 explicitly adjust exchange fees (line 1420: exchangeFeeAdjustment = mulDiv(exchangeFeeAmount, amountInAdjustment, originalAmountIn)) and protocol fees (line 1421: protocolExchangeFeeAdjustment). This asymmetry means the ENTIRE shortfall from partial fill is absorbed by the user while hooks receive 100% of their pre-fill fees. A colluding {pool type + token hook} on a SingleProviderPoolType can systematically extract: hook charges large flat fee, pool consistently partial-fills, hook keeps full fee, user absorbs disproportionate loss.
grounded_in: code-observation: _storeHookFees at lines 2871/2887 writes to persistent storage (tokensOwed mapping via AMMModule.sol:2988) inside _applySwapByOutputOutputFees (line 1537), which executes BEFORE the pool type call at line 1548. Once written, there is no mechanism to decrement or reverse these entries.

code-observation: Input swap partial fill adjustment (lines 1413-1427) proportionally adjusts exchangeFeeAmount (line 1425) and protocolFeeFromFees (line 1426) using mulDiv ratio. Output swap partial fill (lines 1569-1582) adjusts ONLY adjustedAmountSpecified and amountOut — no analogous hook fee adjustment exists.

EXP-9: State committed before completion — hook fees are committed to persistent storage before the pool type determines actual execution, analogous to read-only reentrancy where committed state is observed before final validation.
code-observation: SingleProviderPoolType can partial fill by design (line 1565: only first hop can partial fill, verified at line 1409/1566)

coupled_pair.state_a: tokensOwed[hookFeeKey] — committed at lines 2871/2887 based on ORIGINAL amountOut before pool type call
coupled_pair.state_b: swapCache.amountOut — reduced by partial fill at line 1577 to actualAmountOut after pool type call
coupled_pair.invariant: Hook fees committed to storage must correspond to the actual trade volume after partial fill adjustment

masking_code.masks_invariant: Partial fill check at line 1572 prevents amountOutAdjustment from exceeding adjustedAmountSpecified but does NOT check or adjust the irrevocable hook fees stored 40 lines earlier

hypotheses.title: Unbounded Hook Fees During collectFees Can Drain LP — hookFee Not Bounded by Collected Fees
hypotheses.mechanism: In _positionCollectFees, the pool type returns (positionId, fees0, fees1) representing the LP's accrued trading fees. Then _executeLiquidityCollectFeesHooks is called, returning hookFee0 and hookFee1 from up to 4 hook tiers (token0 hook, token1 hook, position hook, pool hook). The check at the maxHookFee validation only compares against the caller-supplied maxHookFee0/maxHookFee1 parameters. There is NO validation that hookFee0 <= fees0. Net distribution to LP: -fees0.toInt256() + hookFee0.toInt256(). If hookFee0 > fees0, this becomes POSITIVE, meaning the LP must SEND tokens to the AMM during fee collection. A malicious token hook returning hookFee0 = 10000 when fees0 = 100 would extract 9900 tokens from the LP. The LP expected to receive 100 tokens but instead sends 9900. The extracted tokens go to the hook via _storeHookFees. Many DeFi UIs and aggregator integrations set maxHookFee to type(uint256).max as a default. Combined with typical infinite token approvals, the LP is silently drained.
grounded_in: code-observation: Net distribution at AMMModule.sol:353 is `-fees0.toInt256() + hookFee0.toInt256()`. No check enforces hookFee0 <= fees0. When hookFee0 > fees0, the result is positive, triggering _distributeOrCollectLiquidityToken to call _collectToken (transferFrom LP to AMM).

code-observation: maxHookFee validation at line 338 (`hookFee0 <= maxHookFee0`) delegates security entirely to caller parameter choice — the protocol does NOT enforce any relationship between collected fees and hook fees.

EXP-14: Diamond proxy extension hijacker — the hook system (token hooks, pool hooks, liquidity hooks) is the diamond's extension mechanism. A malicious hook exploits unbounded return values to extract funds from LPs through the fee collection path.

Solodit: Bunni v2 TOB-BUNNI-15/16/17/18 (Trail of Bits) — delta sign inversion in Uniswap v4 hooks caused free swaps and positive-sum round trips. Same pattern: unbounded hook return values crossing the trust boundary between protocol and extension.

coupled_pair.state_a: fees0 from pool type collectFees (LP's legitimately earned trading fees)
coupled_pair.state_b: hookFee0 from hook validation (arbitrary uint256, bounded only by caller's maxHookFee parameter)
coupled_pair.invariant: Hook fees during fee collection should not exceed the fees being collected, or at minimum the protocol should enforce an upper bound

masking_code.masks_invariant: maxHookFee0 check at line 338 appears to protect the LP but actually delegates all security to the caller's parameter choice, which defaults to max in most integrations

hypotheses.title: Flash Loan Fee Basis Override — Token Hook Returns tokenFeeAmount=1 to Near-Eliminate Flash Loan Costs
hypotheses.mechanism: In _flashLoan (AMMModule.sol:3288-3382), the fee calculation at lines 3298-3303 has two paths: (1) When tokenFeeAmount == 0 (no hook fee): feeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(loanAmount, flashLoanBPS, MAX_BPS) — the fee is based on the LOAN AMOUNT. (2) When tokenFeeAmount > 0 (hook sets a fee): feeAmount = tokenFeeAmount + mulDivRoundingUp(tokenFeeAmount, flashLoanBPS, MAX_BPS) — the fee is based on the HOOK'S FEE AMOUNT, not the loan amount. In path (2), the protocol's flashLoanBPS is applied as a percentage of the hook's fee, not the loan. If a token hook returns tokenFeeAmount=1 (1 wei), then: feeAmount = 1 + mulDivRoundingUp(1, flashLoanBPS, 10000) = 1 + 1 = 2 wei (for any flashLoanBPS > 0). For a 1,000,000 token loan with flashLoanBPS=30 (0.3%): path (1) would charge 3000 tokens; path (2) charges 2 wei. The protocol fee at line 3373-3378: _storeProtocolFees(feeToken, feeAmount - tokenFeeAmount) = _storeProtocolFees(feeToken, 1 wei). A token owner deploys a hook that returns tokenFeeAmount=1 for flash loans (via TOKEN_SETTINGS_FLASHLOANS_FLAG at Constants.sol:119). All flash loans of that token pay ~1 wei instead of the intended percentage-based fee. The token owner could simultaneously be the flash loan borrower, getting near-free capital access.
grounded_in: code-observation: Conditional at AMMModule.sol:3299 switches fee computation basis. Path tokenFeeAmount==0 at line 3300 uses `loanAmount` as base. Path tokenFeeAmount>0 at line 3302 uses `tokenFeeAmount` as base. These produce VASTLY different results: for loanAmount=1e18, flashLoanBPS=30, tokenFeeAmount=1: path1=3e14, path2=2.

code-observation: Token hooks are set by token owners via setTokenSettings (ModuleAdmin.sol:272). The TOKEN_SETTINGS_FLASHLOANS_FLAG (Constants.sol:119) enables the flash loan hook. The hook's returned tokenFeeAmount has no minimum bound — only the fee token address is validated if non-zero.

EXP-14: Diamond proxy extension hijacker — the token hook system allows token owners to override core protocol fee logic. The fee calculation delegates to the hook, which can return a value that nullifies the protocol's intended fee structure.

coupled_pair.state_a: flashLoanBPS (protocol-set fee rate, intended to apply to loanAmount)
coupled_pair.state_b: tokenFeeAmount (hook-returned value, used as the new fee basis when > 0)
coupled_pair.invariant: Protocol flash loan fee should be proportional to the loan amount, not substitutable by a hook returning an arbitrary (possibly minimal) value

masking_code.masks_invariant: The addition `tokenFeeAmount + mulDivRoundingUp(tokenFeeAmount, flashLoanBPS, MAX_BPS)` appears to add protocol fee ON TOP of hook fee, masking that the protocol fee base changed from loanAmount to tokenFeeAmount

hypotheses.title: Non-Token Hook Fee Storage Key Uses tokenFor Twice — Mismatch with Read/Collect API
hypotheses.mechanism: In AMMModule._storeNonTokenHookFees (lines 3011-3026), the function signature is (address hook, address tokenFor, uint256 feeAmount) — it has NO tokenFee parameter. The storage key at line 3018 is computed as: EfficientHash.efficientHash(hook, EfficientHash.efficientHash(tokenFor, tokenFor)) — tokenFor appears TWICE. However, _transferHookFeesByHook (line 3116-3139) and the view function getHookFeesOwedByHook (ModuleFeeCollection.sol:171-181) compute keys as: hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)) with SEPARATE tokenFor and tokenFee parameters. For current call patterns (liquidity hooks at lines 790/794/838/842/1160/1164/1220/1224), hookFee0 is always stored for token0 and hookFee1 for token1, so tokenFor==tokenFee matches. But _storeNonTokenHookFees is a GENERAL function available to position/pool hooks. If a pool hook or position hook that receives cross-token fees is ever deployed (hookFee denominated in tokenFee != tokenFor), the fees would be stored at hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFor)) but the hook would call collectHookFeesByHook(tokenFor, tokenFee, ...) which reads hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)) — a DIFFERENT key. Fees become permanently locked in the AMM's tokensOwed mapping.
grounded_in: code-observation: _storeNonTokenHookFees at AMMModule.sol:3011 has signature (address hook, address tokenFor, uint256 feeAmount) — 3 params, no tokenFee. Storage key at line 3018: hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFor)). _transferHookFeesByHook at line 3116 has signature (address hook, address tokenFor, address tokenFee, address recipient, uint256 amount) — 5 params. Key at line 3125: hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)). When tokenFor != tokenFee, keys differ.

code-observation: getHookFeesOwedByHook at ModuleFeeCollection.sol:176-178 exposes both tokenFor and tokenFee as separate parameters, confirming the API design intent supports tokenFor != tokenFee scenarios.

EXP-14: Diamond proxy state desync — storage key derivation in the write path (_storeNonTokenHookFees) uses a different formula than the read path (_transferHookFeesByHook/getHookFeesOwedByHook), creating a latent mismatch that manifests when cross-token hook fees are introduced.

coupled_pair.state_a: tokensOwed[hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFor))] — written by _storeNonTokenHookFees at line 3020
coupled_pair.state_b: tokensOwed[hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee))] — read by _transferHookFeesByHook at line 3129
coupled_pair.invariant: Storage key used to write hook fees must match the storage key used to read/collect them

masking_code.masks_invariant: _storeNonTokenHookFees omits the tokenFee parameter entirely, implicitly assuming tokenFor==tokenFee. This assumption holds for current callers but creates a hard constraint that isn't documented or enforced by the API

hypotheses.title: Token Settings Change Leaves Old Hook's Accumulated Fees Socially Inaccessible
hypotheses.mechanism: ModuleAdmin.setTokenSettings (line 272-297) overwrites tokenSettings.packedSettings and tokenSettings.tokenHook (lines 293-294) without migrating or draining the old hook's accumulated fees. If the old hook had TOKEN_SETTINGS_HOOK_MANAGES_FEES_FLAG set (Constants.sol:116), its fees are stored at hash(oldHookAddress, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)). Technically, the old hook CAN still call collectHookFeesByHook since msg.sender is the key — no on-chain blocker exists. However, many hooks are stateless execution contracts (no admin functions, no self-serve collection) designed to be called only by the AMM during swap/liquidity operations. Once deregistered, the AMM no longer calls the old hook, and the hook has no mechanism to initiate collection. The tokens remain in the AMM's balance tracked under tokensOwed but become effectively unclaimable. Repeated hook changes compound the issue: each change orphans the previous hook's fees. The AMM's actual token balance diverges from (reserves + feeBalances + claimable tokensOwed), creating phantom liquidity. If the MODE changes from HOOK_MANAGES_FEES to token-managed (or vice versa), the old-mode fees at the old key are also orphaned.
grounded_in: code-observation: setTokenSettings at ModuleAdmin.sol:293-294 directly overwrites storage without checking Storage.appStorage().tokensOwed for outstanding balances under the old hook's key. No migration function exists.

code-observation: _storeHookFees at AMMModule.sol:2977-2982 branches on TOKEN_SETTINGS_HOOK_MANAGES_FEES_FLAG. When flag is set, key = hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)). When unset, key = hash(TOKEN_MANAGED_HOOK_FEE, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)). Changing the flag changes which key NEW fees use, orphaning old-key balances.

code-observation: collectHookFeesByHook at ModuleFeeCollection.sol:80 passes msg.sender as `hook` to _transferHookFeesByHook. Only the exact old hook address can claim its fees. If the old hook contract lacks a mechanism to call collectHookFeesByHook, funds are permanently locked.

coupled_pair.state_a: tokensOwed[hash(oldHook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee))] — accumulated fees under old hook, persists after change
coupled_pair.state_b: tokenSettings[token].tokenHook — overwritten to new hook at ModuleAdmin.sol:294
coupled_pair.invariant: Hook fee storage should remain accessible when token settings change, or accumulated fees should be drained before hook migration
